definitions.median_c5: close five sessions later ÷ next-session open − 1
definitions.ci_pct_dump: 95% bootstrap interval, 1000 resamples of whole dates
definitions.lift_dump: study dump rate ÷ dump rate of all rows where the condition could be evaluated

caveats: Conditional base rates, not a trading system: no borrow, fees or slippage.
Universe = names listed today (survivorship bias); delisted collapses are missing.
Filing-based studies only cover names with SEC filing history in the data.

baseline.title: All eligible name-days
baseline.condition: every labeled row (price ≥ $0.10, 20-day median $ volume ≥ $50k, ≥ 60 prior sessions)
baseline.plain: Across every eligible small/micro-cap session (1,728,994 cases across 3,373 stocks), the next session fell 5%+ from open to close 9.1% of the time (95% CI 8.7%–9.5%). Median open→close -0.1%; it closed below its open 51.2% of the time and squeezed 20%+ above the open 1.2% of the time. It also RAN UP 5%+ open→close 7.9% of the time (1.00× normal) — so this is mostly a bigger-move signal, not a clean downside one.

studies.title: All eligible name-days
studies.condition: every labeled row (price ≥ $0.10, 20-day median $ volume ≥ $50k, ≥ 60 prior sessions)

studies.title: Up 20%+ on the day
studies.plain: After a stock closed up 20% or more on the day (12,396 cases across 2,139 stocks), the next session fell 5%+ from open to close 38.2% of the time (95% CI 37.1%–39.4%) — 4.21× the 9.1% rate for comparable name-days. Median open→close -2.1%; it closed below its open 57.6% of the time and squeezed 20%+ above the open 15.9% of the time. It also RAN UP 5%+ open→close 25.0% of the time (3.16× normal) — the tilt is to the downside.
